question: Does the financial return associated with athletic investment depend on the type of success?
population: Public Division I programs in the registered Knight-Newhouse 2010-2019 source; outcome-specific observed samples; merged-institution exclusions in primary models

calendar.football_student_demand: fall t, the fall following season t-1; fall t+1 sensitivity

spending_success: lag log total athletics expense -> Cup/100
lag log EADA men's basketball expense -> Sweet16 indicator
primary_families.success_finance: Each of Cup/100, FPI/10, and Sweet16 predicts each of next-year log tickets, log athletics donor contributions, and log net nonallocated-revenue proxy: nine tests
primary_families.flutie: Each success measure predicts log applications and log first-time enrollment at the stated sport-specific fall: six tests

primary_effects: School and contemporaneous basketball-conference-by-year effects; school-clustered covariance, cluster-count-minus-one t intervals
primary_controls: Prior log total enrollment; prior EADA sport participation-category count also in spending models
multiple_testing: Holm adjusted exposure p values within each primary family; all secondary tests explicitly exploratory
basketball_visibility: Sweet16 = at least 64 men's basketball Cup points. Derive zero only after validating an exhaustive sixteen-school positive ledger for each year; retain missing aggregate Cup scores
secondary_checks: Same-sample comparison and joint football/basketball/aggregate models
Spending contemporaneous versus lagged, raw Cup rank and within-year score percentile
Football win percentage and main64 basketball tournament participation
Exact additional-year outcome lag; first differences and school linear trends
Positive-log versus inverse-hyperbolic-sine financial outcomes including observed zeros
Exclude mergers, omit 2015-2017 coach-bonus reporting regime, expense-tail trimming, reported-only IPEDS flags
Historical Power Five versus other FBS programs, 2015-2019; direct interaction tests
Historical prominence from FPI 2005-2008; expanding-window AR(1) outperformance proxy using past information only; describe this as model outperformance rather than known expectations
Leave-one-school-out influence range for selected primary effects
pilot_audit: Attempt 2014-2019 Pearson correlations and school/year FE ticket model on independently obtained data. Report exact sample and timing. Exact reproduction of the claimed 52 schools requires their missing original membership and specification; do not select 52 schools to match reported coefficients.
financial_scope: Net nonallocated revenue proxy = exported total revenue - separate institutional/government support - student fees. Total revenue already nets transfers and expenses may include excess transfers; proxy and balance are not cash profit, gross generated revenue, or causal ROI. Ticket and donor components reported separately.
decision_rule: Report all planned specifications and confidence intervals, including null/negative results; no search or stopping rule based on significance; scenarios remain explicitly hypothetical.
